h1: BK Place Hotel Bueng Kan — an in-town stay with big rooms, easy parking and gentle rates
intro: If you want an in-town place in Bueng Kan that is easy on the wallet, has roomy rooms and is simple to reach by car, BK Place Hotel (BK Place) is a name guests mention often · A 3-star hotel open since 2014 on Bueng Kan-Phang Khon Road by Highway 222, it has around 79 rooms from a wallet-friendly Standard up to VIP · Rooms are clean with big comfortable beds, balconies, fridges and work desks · On site there is a restaurant, a pool and a small kids' water park, plus plenty of parking · From approx ฿450/night.

body.html: BK Place Hotel has been open since 2014, sitting at 168 Moo 9 on Bueng Kan-Phang Khon Road by Highway 222 in the town of Bueng Kan · It is a mid-size hotel of around 79 rooms in a plain block, but what drivers love most is the generous car park — easy to find a space without fighting for one · Being on the main road makes getting in and out of town and driving on to other sights in the province straightforward.

Rooms come in several tiers, from Standard and Superior to Deluxe and VIP/Suite · The Deluxe rooms at around 32 sqm feel genuinely spacious, with a choice of a big bed or twins, and some have a bathtub and a balcony · Guests regularly praise the comfortable beds, clean rooms, cold air-con and the basics being all there — fridge, flat-screen TV, work desk and kettle · The common gripe is that the furniture and rooms look a bit dated compared with the booking-site photos; this is a budget hotel that has been open for several years, so set expectations accordingly.
"Rooms are bigger than expected, the bed is large and comfy, the price is low, there's loads of parking and the staff are helpful — good value for a night in Bueng Kan town."

On site there is a restaurant (Krau BK) serving Thai and Isan food, plus a swimming pool and a small water park with a slide for kids · Families with children tend to like this as the kids get to splash about · It cuts both ways, though: several reviews note that the water park gets fairly noisy from the afternoon until around 8pm, so a room nearby can disturb your rest · A few guests have also found the pool water cloudy on some days, so it is worth checking the pool before you plan to swim properly.

On breakfast, be clear that most room rates do not include it — if you want it, it costs around ฿100/person and is served in the morning · As for location, the hotel is within the town but not right in the riverside walking strip; you will need to drive or grab a ride a few minutes to reach the Mekong riverfront, markets and restaurants in the centre · That makes it better suited to people with their own vehicle than to those who plan to explore on foot.

To be straight about it, BK Place Hotel suits travellers who want a big, clean, affordable room and are driving themselves around Bueng Kan · If you are using the town as a base to drive out to Phu Thok, Naka Cave or Bueng Khong Long and want a good-value bed with easy parking, it fits well · A score of 8.6 from 7 Trip.com reviews reflects that most guests are happy at this price point · The grumbles are the ageing rooms and furniture, the water-park noise in the afternoon, and breakfast costing extra.

A tip from reading the reviews: ask for a room away from the water-park side to dodge the afternoon noise, and if you book through an app, look at the Deluxe rooms — they are noticeably bigger for only a little more than a Standard · Drivers can relax about parking, and if you want breakfast, it is easier to request it at check-in.

honestSummary: BK Place Hotel sells big rooms, low rates and easy parking in the town of Bueng Kan — a strong fit for self-drivers using the town as a base for Phu Thok, Naka Cave or Bueng Khong Long · It has a pool and a kids' water park, and an on-site restaurant · Just accept the ageing rooms, the water-park noise in the afternoon, and breakfast costing extra.
honestChecks: If you want to be on the Mekong riverfront or to explore the town on foot — this hotel is on Highway 222, a short drive from the river → if walking matters, choose a stay closer to the riverfront instead.
If you are serious about quiet during the day — the water park is noisy from the afternoon to around 8pm → ask for a room away from the water-park side at the time of booking.
If you expect brand-new rooms like the photos — the hotel has been open since 2014 and rooms and furniture show their age → treat it as a value stay, not a luxury hotel, and you'll be happier.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — BK Place Hotel Bueng Kan

faq.q: Where is BK Place Hotel in Bueng Kan, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It is at 168 Moo 9 on Bueng Kan-Phang Khon Road by Highway 222, in the town of Bueng Kan · It is about a 5-minute drive to the centre and the Mekong riverfront · It makes a handy base for driving to Phu Thok, Three Whale Rock, Naka Cave and Bueng Khong Long · There is a large free car park, so it is great if you are self-driving.

faq.q: How much does BK Place Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿450/night for a Standard room · Superior is around ฿500 · Deluxe (around 32 sqm, with a bathtub and balcony) is around ฿550 · BK VIP/Suite is around ฿1,000 · Most rates do not include breakfast — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does BK Place Hotel have a swimming pool and a water park?
faq.a: Yes · The hotel has a swimming pool and a small water park with a slide, good for families with children · There is also a restaurant (Krau BK) and a gym on site · Be aware the water park is noisy from the afternoon to around 8pm, and the pool water can be cloudy on some days, so check it before you swim.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at BK Place Hotel — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are spacious with big comfortable beds, clean and with cold air-con, plus a fridge, flat-screen TV, work desk and kettle · Deluxe rooms have a bathtub and a balcony · The common gripe is that the furniture and rooms look dated compared with the booking photos, as this is a value hotel open since 2014.

faq.q: Who is BK Place Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits travellers who want a big, clean, affordable room and are self-driving · Families with kids also like the water park · It works well as a base for Phu Thok, Naka Cave or Bueng Khong Long · If you want to walk the riverfront in town, you'll need to drive in a little.

faq.q: What should I know before booking BK Place Hotel?
faq.a: Most rates do not include breakfast; if you want it, it costs around ฿100/person · The water park is noisy in the afternoon, so ask for a room away from that side · Deluxe rooms cost only a little more than a Standard but are bigger — worth it if you can stretch.
